title: Your first prayer
hook: You don't need to know Arabic to pray today. You need the moves and a few words.

screens.text: Today you pray. You don't need Arabic or a perfect memory. You need the moves and a few short words, and you'll add more every day.
A prayer is made of **rak'ahs** (rounds). One rak'ah: stand, bow, then two prostrations, forehead to the floor. All five prayers are yours from today: pray each with what you know so far.
bubbles: {women}On your period? You don't pray during it, and you don't make those prayers up.{/women}

screens.prompt: How many rak'ahs in each prayer?
screens.text: Fajr has 2. Maghrib has 3. Dhuhr, Asr and Isha have 4. Set each one.

steps.text: Make sure your clothes and the spot where you pray are clean

{men}Cover at least from your navel to your knees.{/men}{women}Cover everything except your face and hands, hair included, in clothes you can't see through. Loose is best. {{masjid.name}} will tell you its view on the feet.{/women}
In your heart, intend the prayer: "I'm praying Dhuhr for Allah."
Make sure your clothes and the spot where you pray are clean
{men}Cover from your navel to your knees, knees included.{/men}{women}Cover everything except your face, hands and feet, hair included, in clothes you can't see through. Loose is best.{/women}
In your heart, intend the prayer: "I'm praying Dhuhr for Allah."

screens.when: To begin the prayer, and as you go down to bow, go down to prostrate, sit up, and stand up for the next rak'ah.

screens.title: Watch one rak'ah
screens.intro: Tap Next move, or Play. Pause until you're still in every position: never rush.

moves.text: Stand facing the qibla. In your heart, intend the prayer.
Raise your hands and say *Allahu akbar*. You're now in prayer: no talking, eating or checking your phone until it ends.
Hold your hands the way {{masjid.name}} teaches: most fold the right over the left. Recite what you know (next screens).
Say *Allahu akbar* and bow: hands on your knees, back flat. Be still and say *Subhan Allah* three times.
Stand back up straight. Pause until you're still.
Say *Allahu akbar* and prostrate: forehead and nose, both hands, both knees and your toes on the floor, toes pointing to the qibla.
Be still and say *Subhan Allah* three times.
Say *Allahu akbar* and sit up. Pause until you're still.
Say *Allahu akbar* and prostrate again. Be still: *Subhan Allah* three times. That's one rak'ah!
Stand facing the qibla. In your heart, intend the prayer.
Raise your hands {men}to your ears{/men}{women}to your shoulders{/women} and say *Allahu akbar*. You're now in prayer: no talking, eating or checking your phone.
Fold your hands, right over left, {men}just below your navel{/men}{women}on your chest{/women}. Recite what you know (next screens).
Say *Allahu akbar* and bow: hands on your knees, back flat. Be still and say *Subhan Allah* three times.
Stand back up straight. Pause until you're still.
Say *Allahu akbar* and go down: knees, then hands, then forehead and nose. **Keep your toes on the floor**, pointing to the qibla.
{men}Elbows off the floor and away from your sides.{/men}{women}Keep your arms and body close together.{/women} Be still and say *Subhan Allah* three times.
Say *Allahu akbar* and sit up. Pause until you're still.
Say *Allahu akbar* and prostrate again. Be still: *Subhan Allah* three times. That's one rak'ah!

screens.text: **Standing: what to say.** The goal is *al-Fatiha*, the Qur'an's first chapter (Days 11–16). Today, say its first line, then the words the Prophet ﷺ taught a man who couldn't yet memorize Qur'an [Abu Dawud 832].
bubbles: Practice them before and after prayer, never from a screen during it.

screens.meaning: All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds
screens.when: While standing, in every rak'ah. It's your first verse of the Qur'an. [Q 1:2]

screens.arabic: سُبْحَانَ ٱللَّٰهِ، وَٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّٰهِ، وَلَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّٰهُ، وَٱللَّٰهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّٰهِ
screens.translit: Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
screens.meaning: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no power or strength except through Allah
screens.when: While standing, after your verse, until you've learned al-Fatiha. If it's too long today, say what you can.

screens.situation: You're standing in your first prayer and your mind goes blank. The words you practiced are gone.

options.text: Say what you do remember, even just "Subhan Allah" or "Allahu akbar," and carry on
options.feedback: That's it. Say what you can and keep going. Mistakes while you're learning aren't sins.

options.text: Stop and look up the words on your phone
options.feedback: Better not. Some scholars say reading from a screen can invalidate the prayer. Use what you remember, and practice afterwards.

options.text: Stop praying until you know it perfectly
options.feedback: Please don't. The prayer is due now, and a learner's effort counts. It gets easier every day.

moves.text: Say *Allahu akbar*, stand, and pray a second rak'ah the same way.
After its second prostration, stay sitting. {{masjid.name}} will show you how to sit.
Say the shahada from Day 1.
moves.say: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah…

moves.text: Turn your head to the right and say *As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah*.
Turn to the left and say it again. Your prayer is done.
Say *Allahu akbar*, stand, and pray a second rak'ah the same way.
After its second prostration, stay sitting: {men}on your left foot, with your right foot upright and its toes toward the qibla{/men}{women}with both feet tucked out to your right{/women}.
Say the shahada from Day 1.
moves.say: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah…

moves.text: Turn your head to the right and say *As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah*.
Turn to the left and say it again. Your prayer is done.

screens.meaning: Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah
screens.when: To end the prayer: once turning right, once turning left.

screens.title: Your whole 2-rak'ah prayer
screens.intro: Watch it once from start to finish before you pray. Press Play, or go move by move.

moves.text: Wudu done, covered, facing the qibla. Intend the prayer in your heart.
Raise your hands: *Allahu akbar*.
Fold your hands. *Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin*, then the remembrance words.
*Allahu akbar*, bow. Be still. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
Stand back up. Be still.
*Allahu akbar*, prostrate, toes on the floor. Be still. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
*Allahu akbar*, sit up. Be still.
*Allahu akbar*, prostrate again. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
*Allahu akbar*, stand for the second rak'ah. Recite again.
*Allahu akbar*, bow. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
Stand back up. Be still.
*Allahu akbar*, prostrate. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
*Allahu akbar*, sit up. Be still.
*Allahu akbar*, prostrate again. *Subhan Allah* ×3.
*Allahu akbar*, sit, and say the shahada.
*As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah*, to the right…
…and to the left. Done!

screens.done_text: You've got it. Now put your phone away and pray.

screens.text: **Maghrib, Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are longer.** After the second rak'ah, sit and say the shahada, but don't end. Say *Allahu akbar*, stand, and pray the rest. Then sit, shahada, salam.

screens.before: At Maghrib, after the first sitting, you stand and pray
screens.after: more rak'ah before the final sitting.

Not quite. That's Dhuhr, Asr and Isha. Maghrib has 3 in all, so 1 more.
Not quite. Maghrib has 3 rak'ahs, so there's 1 more after the first sitting.

screens.text: Stand, bow, prostrate twice, with stillness in each; repeat; sit and end with the salam. Say what you know so far. All five prayers start today.
Your first prayer won't be perfect, and it doesn't need to be. Even someone who stumbles through the Qur'an gets a double reward [Muslim 798]. Slow and steady.

options.feedback: Right. Fajr is 2, Maghrib 3, and the other three are 4.

options.feedback: Right. Say the Qur'an you know, then the phrases the Prophet ﷺ taught [Abu Dawud 832].

options.feedback: Not quite. Pray now with what you know while you learn al-Fatiha.

options.feedback: Not quite. Practice from your phone before and after prayer, not during it.

check.prompt: What should you do in each position: bowing, standing up, prostrating, sitting?

options.feedback: Right. Stillness in each position is part of a proper prayer.

options.text: Move on as quickly as you can
options.feedback: Not quite. Pause until you're still in each position. Rushing can spoil the prayer.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- All five prayers are due from the day of conversion; the convert prays with what they know while learning, and nobody presents fewer prayers as allowed [SeekersGuidance 167692; IslamWeb 529861].
- Women don't pray during menstruation or postnatal bleeding, and don't make those prayers up [First Instructions on Worship ch. 4–5].
- Recitation while learning: say whatever Qur'an you know (today: *Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin*, [Q 1:2]), then the remembrance phrases [Abu Dawud 832; Qibla 35467 (Hanafi: a new Muslim is excused from what they can't yet recite and should learn quickly); Dar al-Ifta Egypt 8030].
- **Stillness (tuma'ninah)** in bowing, standing up from it, prostration and sitting between prostrations is required (wajib in the Hanafi school; a pillar in the others). Teach it every time.
- **Hanafi:** keep at least the toes on the floor during prostration; lifting both feet for the whole prostration spoils it. Men's and women's positions differ as in the lesson [First Instructions on Worship ch. 7].
- **No reading from a card or phone during prayer** until a scholar rules (Hanafis hold it can invalidate the prayer).
- Honest mistakes while learning aren't sins [SeekersGuidance, convert following a school].
- Rak'ahs: Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4.

**Likely questions**
- *"Walk me through a prayer."* Step by step, one message per position, using this lesson's wording and the masjid variant, including stillness and toes on the floor. Offer the 3- and 4-rak'ah versions.
- *"Can I pray in English?"* Not the recitation itself; the verse and phrases are the bridge while learning. Personal du'a in English is welcome outside the prayer. Never offer a translation of al-Fatiha to recite in prayer (Q13).
- *"Someone walked in while I was praying."* Keep going calmly; the prayer is fine. Day 5 covers this.
- *"I'm doing it wrong."* Reassure: learners make mistakes, effort is rewarded, and it gets easier within a week. Suggest praying once with their mentor or at the masjid.
- *"What about witr?"* If the masjid is Hanafi: it's a short prayer after Isha that Day 8 teaches; for now, focus on the five. Don't teach it in detail here (Q18).
- *"I missed prayers before today."* Prayers before Islam aren't made up. About the day they converted, suggest asking the imam (Q15).
- *"I'm on my period."* No prayer until it ends, then ghusl (Day 17). She can still learn the movements and words.

**Escalate:** physical limitations (can't stand, kneel or prostrate: give the general idea that one prays sitting or as able, and send details to the imam); the day-of-conversion question (Q15).

**Don't**
- Don't say "start with one prayer a day" or anything like it (Q4).
- Don't say "until you learn, just sit and thank Allah" (*Welcome to Islam*'s advice; Q11).
- Don't suggest reading from the phone during prayer (Q2).
- Don't overload with sunnah prayers or extra du'as; they come later.
madhabNote:
Other schools differ in small, valid ways:
- **Hands:** Shafi'is fold them above the navel; Malikis usually leave them at their sides in obligatory prayers.
- **Raising the hands:** Shafi'is and Hanbalis also raise them before and after bowing.
- **Sitting:** in the final sitting, Malikis and Shafi'is sit with the left foot tucked under and the hip on the floor (Hanbalis do this only in prayers of 3 or 4 rak'ahs); Hanafi men sit on the left foot.
- **Before al-Fatiha is learned:** every school says to learn it quickly. Shafi'is and Hanbalis say to recite whatever Qur'an you know first, then remembrance phrases for the rest; in the Hanafi school, one verse is required and a new Muslim is excused while learning. Today's verse plus the phrases covers them.
